bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷一百〇六 漢書8: 列傳三 王周 劉審交 武漢球 張瓘 李殷 劉在明 馬萬 李彥從 郭謹 皇甫立 白再榮 張鵬
title.en: Volume 106 Book of Later Jin 8: Biographies 3 - Wang Zhou, Liu Shenjiao, Wu Hanqiu, Zhang Guan, Li Yin, Liu Zaiming, Ma Wan, Li Yancong, Guo Jin, Huang Fuli, Bai Zairong, Zhang Peng
title.raw: 卷一百〇六 漢書8: 列傳三 王周 劉審交 武漢球 張瓘 李殷 劉在明 馬萬 李彥從 郭謹 皇甫立 白再榮 張鵬 Volume 106 Book of Later Jin 8: Biographies 3 - Wang Zhou, Liu Shenjiao, Wu Hanqiu, Zhang Guan, Li Yin, Liu Zaiming, Ma Wan, Li Yancong, Guo Jin, Huang Fuli, Bai Zairong, Zhang Peng

sentences.zh: 王周，魏州人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhou was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou came from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少勇健，從軍事唐莊宗、明宗，稍遷裨校，以戰功累歷郡守。

translations.literal: In youth he was brave and robust; he followed the armies in the service of Tang Zhuangzong and Mingzong, was gradually promoted to deputy commander, and through battle achievements successively held commandery governorships.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and sturdy. He soldiered under Tang Zhuangzong and Mingzong, rose step by step through the officer ranks, and earned a series of prefectural posts on the strength of his battlefield record.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，範延光叛於魏州，周從楊光遠攻降之，安重榮以鎮州叛，從杜重威討平之，以功授貝州節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jin Tianfu era, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Weizhou; Zhou followed Yang Guangyuan to attack and subdue him; An Chongrong rebelled with Zhenzhou; Zhou followed Du Chongwei to suppress and pacify him, and for merit was appointed military governor of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin Tianfu reign, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Weizhou. Zhou marched with Yang Guangyuan to crush him, then joined Du Chongwei against An Chongrong's revolt at Zhenzhou. For these services he was made military governor of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，移鎮涇州。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was transferred to govern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was reassigned to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，前帥張彥澤在任苛虐，部民逃者五千餘戶，及下車，革前弊二十餘事，逃民歸復，賜詔褒美。

translations.literal: Previously, the former governor Zhang Yanzhe had been harsh and cruel in office, and more than five thousand households of the circuit's people had fled; when Zhou took up his post, he reformed more than twenty former abuses, the fugitive people returned, and an edict was bestowed praising him.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor Zhang Yanzhe had ruled with harsh cruelty, driving more than five thousand households to flee. When Zhou arrived he abolished more than twenty abuses of the old regime; the refugees came back, and the court issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 後歷鄧、陜二鎮。

translations.literal: Later he successively governed the two circuits of Deng and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He later held governorships in Deng and Shan in turn.

sentences.zh: 陽城之役，周時為定州節度使，大軍往來，供饋無闕，未幾，遷鎮州節度使。

translations.literal: At the Yangcheng campaign, Zhou was then military governor of Dingzhou; the great army came and went, and provisions were supplied without shortfall; before long he was transferred to military governor of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yangcheng campaign Zhou was military governor of Dingzhou. He kept the main armies supplied without fail and was soon moved to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 周稟性寬惠，人庶便之。

translations.literal: Zhou's nature was lenient and generous, and the people found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was by nature mild and generous, and the common people benefited from his rule.

sentences.zh: 開運末，杜重威降於契丹，引契丹主臨城諭之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyun era, Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan and brought the Khitan ruler to the city to announce it to them.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Kaiyun reign Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan and brought the Khitan ruler before the walls to address the garrison.

sentences.zh: 周泣曰：「受國重恩，不能死戰，而以兵降，何面南行見人主與士大夫乎？

translations.literal: Zhou wept and said: "I have received the state's heavy grace; I could not die fighting, yet I surrender my troops—what face have I to go south and meet the sovereign and the scholar-officials?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou wept and said, "The state loaded me with favor, yet I could not die in battle and instead surrender my troops—how can I face south to meet the emperor and the scholar-officials?"

sentences.zh: 」乃痛飲欲引決，家人止之。

translations.literal: " He then drank heavily intending to take his own life, but his family restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: " He drank himself into a stupor and tried to kill himself, but his household stopped him.

sentences.zh: 事不獲已，乃見契丹主，授鄧州節度使、檢校太師。

translations.literal: The matter could not be helped; he then met the Khitan ruler and was appointed military governor of Dengzhou and honorary Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Left with no choice, he went before the Khitan ruler and was given Dengzhou and the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 高祖定天下，移鎮徐州，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu settled the realm, Zhou was transferred to Xuzhou and given the additional title of Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu secured the empire, Zhou was moved to Xuzhou and made associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年二月，以疾卒於鎮，輟視朝二日，贈中書令。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianyou, he died of illness at his post; court audiences were suspended for two days, and he was posthumously given the title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Qianyou 1 he died of illness in office. The court halted audiences for two days and posthumously made him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周性寬恕，不忤物情。

translations.literal: Zhou's nature was forgiving and he did not go against people's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was forgiving by nature and never needlessly offended others.

sentences.zh: 初刺信都，州城西橋敗，覆民租車，周曰：「橋梁不飭，刺史之過也。

translations.literal: When he first governed Xindu, the western bridge of the prefectural city collapsed and overturned the people's tax-grain carts; Zhou said: "The bridge was not maintained—that is the prefect's fault."
translations.idiomatic: On his first appointment at Xindu the city bridge on the west side collapsed and capsized carts carrying the people's tax grain. Zhou said, "A bridge in disrepair is the prefect's fault."

sentences.zh: 」乃還其所沈粟，出私財以修之，民庶悅焉。

translations.literal: He then returned the grain that had sunk, spent his private wealth to repair it, and the people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the sunk grain to the owners, paid for repairs out of his own purse, and won the people's approval.

sentences.zh: 劉審交，字求益，幽州文安人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shenjiao, styled Qiuyi, was a native of Wen'an in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shenjiao, courtesy name Qiuyi, came from Wen'an in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖海，父師遂。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Hai; his father Shisui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Liu Hai and his father Liu Shisui.

sentences.zh: 審交少讀書，尤精吏道，起家署北平主簿，轉興唐令，本府召補牙職。

translations.literal: Shenjiao in youth studied books and was especially skilled in administrative matters; he began his career as secretary of Beiping, was transferred to magistrate of Xingtang, and the headquarters summoned him to fill a staff post in the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjiao read widely in his youth and excelled at official routine. He began as secretary at Beiping, became magistrate of Xingtang, and was then called to a staff post at the circuit headquarters.

sentences.zh: 劉守光之僭號，偽署兵部尚書，燕亡，歸於太原。

translations.literal: When Liu Shouguang usurped the title, he was falsely appointed Minister of War; when Yan fell, he returned to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shouguang declared himself emperor, Shenjiao was given the false title of Minister of War. After Yan fell he went back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 莊宗知之，用為諸府從事。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong knew of him and employed him as staff officer in various offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong knew his ability and used him on the staffs of several bureaus.

sentences.zh: 同光初，趙德鈞鎮幽州，朝廷以內官馬紹宏為北面轉運使，辟審交為判官。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Tongguang, Zhao Dejun held Youzhou; the court appointed the inner attendant Ma Shaohong as north-front transport commissioner, and Shenjiao was recruited as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang, Zhao Dejun governed Youzhou. The court sent the eunuch Ma Shaohong as north-front transport commissioner and recruited Shenjiao as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 王都據定州叛，朝廷命王晏球進討，以審交為轉運供軍使，王都平，以勞授遼州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Du held Dingzhou in rebellion; the court ordered Wang Yanqiu to advance and attack, with Shenjiao as transport and supply commissioner for the army; when Wang Du was pacified, he was given Lingzhou prefect for his labors.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Du rebelled at Dingzhou the court sent Wang Yanqiu to suppress him, with Shenjiao as army transport and supply commissioner. After Dingzhou was pacified he was rewarded with the prefecture of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，復為北面供軍轉運使，改磁州刺史，以母年高，去官就養。

translations.literal: The next year he again served as north-front army supply transport commissioner, was changed to Cizhou prefect, and because his mother was advanced in years left office to go and support her.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again served as north-front supply commissioner, then became prefect of Ci. When his mother grew old he resigned to care for her at home.

sentences.zh: 及丁內艱，毀瘠過禮，服闋，不出累年。

translations.literal: When he completed mourning for his mother he wasted his body beyond the rites; after the mourning period ended he did not go out for many years.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he grieved beyond what ritual required. When the mourning ended he stayed secluded for years.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖踐阼，範延光以魏州叛，命楊光遠以總兵討之，復召審交為供饋使。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu ascended the throne, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Weizhou; Yang Guangyuan was ordered to command the army in total to suppress him, and Shenjiao was again summoned as supply commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Weizhou. Yang Guangyuan was put in overall command to crush the revolt, and Shenjiao was again called up as supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鄴中平，命審交為三司使，授右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Yezhong was pacified, Shenjiao was appointed Commissioner of the Three Departments and given the post of General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Yezhong fell he was made Commissioner of the Three Departments and General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，出為陳州防禦使，歲餘，移襄州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year he went out as defender of Chenzhou; after more than a year he was moved to defender of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year he left the capital to defend Chenzhou. A year later he was transferred to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 審交治襄、漢，撫綏有術，民庶懷之。

translations.literal: Shenjiao governed Xiang and Han with skill in soothing and settling; the people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiang and Han he governed with a gift for reassurance and settlement, and the people held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 青州楊光遠平，降平盧軍為防禦州，復用審交為防禦使，累官至檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou was pacified, Pinglu army was reduced to a defense prefecture; Shenjiao was again used as defender, and he rose in office to honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Guangyuan's defeat at Qingzhou, Pinglu was reduced to a defense command. Shenjiao was again made defender there and eventually rose to honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 時用軍之後，審交矜恤撫理，雕弊復蘇。

translations.literal: At a time when the army had just been used, Shenjiao showed compassion in soothing and governing, and the devastated regions revived.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of war he governed with compassionate care, and ruined districts began to recover.

sentences.zh: 契丹破晉，審交以代歸，蕭翰在都，復用為三司使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Shenjiao returned from the north; Xiao Han was in the capital and again employed him as Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan overthrew Jin, Shenjiao came back from the north. Xiao Han held the capital and again made him Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 翰歸蕃，李從益在汴州，召高行周、武行德將委以軍事，皆不受命。

translations.literal: When Han returned to his tribe, Li Congyi was at Bianzhou; he summoned Gao Xingzhou and Wu Xingde to entrust them with military affairs, but both refused the orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Han went back to his people, Li Congyi was at Bian. He tried to put Gao Xingzhou and Wu Xingde in charge of the army, but neither would accept.

sentences.zh: 尋聞高祖起義於太原，史宏肇在澤潞，都人大懼。

translations.literal: Soon word came that Gaozu had raised arms at Taiyuan; Shi Hongzhao was at Ze and Lu, and the people of the capital were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Word soon came that Gaozu had risen at Taiyuan while Shi Hongzhao held Ze and Lu. The capital was gripped by fear.

sentences.zh: 時有燕軍千人守捉諸門，李從益母王淑妃詢於文武臣僚曰：「予子母在洛，孤危自處，一旦為蕭翰所逼，致令及此。

translations.literal: At that time a thousand men of the Yan army guarded the gates; Li Congyi's mother, the Honored Consort Wang Shufei, inquired of the civil and military officials: "My son and I are in Luozhou, isolated and in peril; we have been driven to this by Xiao Han.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand Yan troops then held the gates. Li Congyi's mother, Consort Wang Shufei, asked the civil and military officials, "My son and I are stranded in Luoyang, helpless and exposed. Xiao Han has forced us into this plight.

sentences.zh: 但遣人迎請太原，勿以予子母為事。

translations.literal: Only send someone to welcome Taiyuan—do not make my son and me the issue."
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to welcome Taiyuan and do not make my son and me your concern."

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「收拾諸處守營兵士與燕軍，足以把城，以俟河北救應可也。

translations.literal: Someone said: "Gather the garrison troops from the various posts together with the Yan army— that is enough to hold the city and wait for rescue from Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: One man said, "Rally the garrison troops everywhere with the Yan force—we can hold the city and wait for help from Hebei."

sentences.zh: 」妃曰：「非謀也，我子母亡國之餘，安敢與人爭天下！

translations.literal: The consort said: "That is not a plan. My son and I are remnants of a fallen state—how dare we contend with others for the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: The consort replied, "That is no plan. My son and I are all that is left of a ruined house—how dare we fight others for the empire!"

sentences.zh: 」眾議籍籍，猶以把城為詞。

translations.literal: The crowd debated noisily, still speaking of holding the city.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly buzzed with argument, many still insisting on defending the walls.

sentences.zh: 審交曰：「余燕人也，今城有燕軍，固合為燕謀，然事機有所不可。

translations.literal: Shenjiao said: "I am a man of Yan; now there are Yan troops in the city, so it is fitting to plot for Yan—but there are things the situation will not allow.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjiao said, "I am a Yan man myself, and with Yan troops in the city it would seem right to plot for Yan. Yet circumstances forbid it.

sentences.zh: 此城經敵軍破除之後，民力空匱，餘眾幸存，若更謀之不臧，閉門拒守，一月之內，無復遺類。

translations.literal: This city, after the enemy army broke and destroyed it, has its people's strength emptied and depleted; only a remnant survives. If you plot further without success and shut the gates to resist, within a month there will be no one left.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has already smashed this city and drained its people. Only a remnant survives. Another ill-judged plan to bar the gates and resist will, within a month, leave no one alive.

sentences.zh: 諸君勿言，宜從太妃處分。

translations.literal: Gentlemen, speak no more of it; you should follow the Honored Consort's decision."
translations.idiomatic: Say no more, gentlemen. Do as the consort directs."

sentences.zh: 」繇是從益遣使往太原貢奉。

translations.literal: Because of this Congyi sent envoys to Taiyuan to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On this advice Congyi sent envoys to Taiyuan with tribute.

sentences.zh: 高祖至汴，罷使歸班。

translations.literal: When Gaozu reached Bian, Shenjiao was dismissed from his commission and returned to the regular roster.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu reached Bian, Shenjiao was relieved of his special commission and returned to ordinary service.

sentences.zh: 隱帝嗣位，用為汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, Shenjiao was made defender of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yin he was appointed defender of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 汝為近輔，號為難治，審交盡去煩弊，無擾於民，百姓歌之。

translations.literal: Ru was a near capital circuit and was called hard to govern; Shenjiao removed all troublesome abuses and did not disturb the people, and the common people sang his praise.
translations.idiomatic: Ru lay close to the capital and had a reputation for being unruly. Shenjiao swept away vexatious abuses, left the people unmolested, and they sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 乾祐二年春，卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Qianyou he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianyou 2 he died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 郡人聚哭柩前所，列狀乞留葬本州界，立碑起祠，以時致祭。

translations.literal: The people of the command gathered to weep before his coffin and submitted a petition asking that he be buried within the borders of this prefecture, with a stele erected and a shrine built, and sacrifices offered at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery's people wept before his coffin and petitioned to bury him within their borders, erect a stele, build a shrine, and offer seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 本州以聞，詔曰：「朝廷之制，皆有舊章，牧守之官，比無贈典。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported it; an edict said: "The court's regulations all have old statutes; for governors and prefects there has generally been no posthumous award.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported upward. An edict said, "The court's rules all rest on ancient precedent, and prefects and governors are not usually honored after death.

sentences.zh: 其或政能殊異，惠及蒸黎，生有令名，沒留遺愛，褒賢獎善，豈限彜章。

translations.literal: If one's governance is exceptionally outstanding and one's kindness reaches the black-haired people, if in life one has a fine name and in death one leaves enduring affection, to praise the worthy and reward the good—how can that be limited to the standard code?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet when a man's rule is truly exceptional, his kindness reaches the people, his name in life is bright and his love survives him, to praise worth and reward goodness cannot be bound by ordinary statute."

sentences.zh: 可特贈太尉，吏民所請宜依。

translations.literal: He may specially be given the posthumous title of Grand Marshal; what the officials and people request should be granted as asked."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be specially posthumously made Grand Marshal, and grant what the officials and people ask."

sentences.zh: 」故相國、太師、秦國公馮道聞之曰：「予嘗為劉汝州僚佐，知其為人廉平慈善，無害之良吏也。

translations.literal: The former chief minister, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Qin, Feng Dao, on hearing it said: "I once served as Liu of Ruzhou's subordinate and knew him to be a incorrupt, fair, and charitable man, a harmless good official.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief minister and Grand Preceptor Feng Dao, Duke of Qin, said on hearing the news, "I once served under Liu of Ruzhou and knew him as an honest, fair, and kindly man—a harmless magistrate of the best sort.

sentences.zh: 刺遼、磁，治陳、襄、青，皆稱平允，不顯殊尤，其理汝也，又安有異哉！

translations.literal: In governing Ling and Ci, and in administering Chen, Xiang, and Qing, he was all called even-handed; he showed no special excellence, and in governing Ru as well—how could there have been anything different!"
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Ling and Ci and as defender of Chen, Xiang, and Qing he was always called even-handed, without flashy distinction. His rule at Ru was no different.

sentences.zh: 民之租賦不能減也，徭役不能息也，寒者不能衣也，餒者不能食也，百姓自汲汲然，而使君何有於我哉！

translations.literal: The people's land tax could not be reduced, corvée labor could not be stilled, the cold could not be clothed, the hungry could not be fed—the common people toiled on their own account; what did the magistrate have to do with us!"
translations.idiomatic: Peasant rents could not be cut, labor levies could not cease, the cold went unclothed and the hungry unfed. The people hurried about their own affairs—what did the magistrate do for us!"

sentences.zh: 然身死之日，致黎民懷感如此者，誠以不行鞭樸，不行刻剝，不因公而循私，不害物以利己，確然行良吏之事，薄罰宥過，謹身節用，安俸祿、守禮分而已。

translations.literal: Yet at the day of his death the common people were moved to such feeling—truly because he did not apply the whip, did not practice harsh exaction, did not use public office to pursue private ends, did not harm things to benefit himself, but steadfastly performed the affairs of a good official: light punishment and pardon for faults, careful self-restraint and frugality, contentment with salary and observance of ritual propriety, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at his death the people mourned him so warmly because he never wielded the lash or practiced harsh levies, never bent public duty to private gain or harmed others for his own profit, but simply did what a good official does: light penalties, mercy for faults, restraint, thrift, living on his salary and keeping to his station.

sentences.zh: 凡從事於斯者，孰不能乎！

translations.literal: Whoever engages in this—who cannot do it!"
translations.idiomatic: Whoever holds such an office cannot do the same?"

sentences.zh: 但前之守土者不能如是，是以汝民咨嗟愛慕。

translations.literal: Only the former holders of the land could not be like this, and therefore the people of Ru sighed and loved him in longing.
translations.idiomatic: Only earlier governors had failed to do so, and that is why the people of Ru sighed and cherished his memory.

sentences.zh: 今天下戎馬之後，四方兇盜之餘，杼柚空而賦斂繁，人民稀而倉稟匱，謂之康泰，未易輕言。

translations.literal: Today, after war-horses across the realm and amid the remnants of bandits in the four directions, the loom is empty while levies are heavy, the people are few while granaries are depleted—to call it peace and prosperity is not something to say lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after armies have trampled the empire and robbers still haunt the four quarters, looms stand idle while taxes press hard, people are few and storehouses bare—to speak lightly of peace and plenty is impossible.

sentences.zh: 侯伯牧宰，若能哀矜之，不至聚斂，不殺無辜之民，民為邦本，政為民本，和平寬易，即劉君之政安足稱耶！

translations.literal: If the feudal lords and governors can show compassion and not press to extortion, not kill innocent people, taking the people as the foundation of the state and government as the foundation of the people, with peace, leniency, and ease—then is Liu Jun's government worth praising!"
translations.idiomatic: If regional lords and governors can pity the people, refrain from crushing levies, and spare the innocent—making the people the root of the state and government the root of the people, with peace, leniency, and ease—then is Liu Jun's rule even worth mentioning!"

sentences.zh: 復河患不至於令名哉！

translations.literal: Would restoring the Yellow River's harm not reach a fine name!"
translations.idiomatic: Would he not win a great name simply by keeping the Yellow River from harming the people!"

sentences.zh: 」道仍為著哀詞六章，鐫於墓碑之陰焉。

translations.literal: Dao still composed six stanzas of mourning verse and had them carved on the reverse of the tomb stele.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao also wrote six stanzas of mourning verse and had them cut into the back of the tomb stele.

sentences.zh: 武漢球，澤州人也。

translations.literal: Wu Hanqiu was a native of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hanqiu came from Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 少拳勇，潞帥李嗣昭倚為親信，事唐莊宗、明宗，繼為禁軍裨校。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in boxing and courage; the Lu governor Li Sizhao relied on him as a trusted intimate; he served Tang Zhuangzong and Mingzong and successively held posts as deputy commander of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was strong in boxing and boldness. Li Sizhao of Lu made him a trusted confidant. He served Zhuangzong and Mingzong and rose through the ranks of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，會晉高祖引契丹為援，與朝廷隔絕，遂歸晉祖。

translations.literal: In Qingtai, when Jin Gaozu brought the Khitan as allies and was cut off from the court, he then submitted to the Jin founder.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai, when Jin Gaozu allied with the Khitan and was cut off from the Later Tang court, Hanqiu went over to him.

sentences.zh: 天福初，授趙州刺史，入為奉國軍都指揮使，出刺曹州。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Tianfu he was given Zhao prefect, entered the capital as commander of the Fengguo Army, and went out to govern Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu he became prefect of Zhao, then commander of the Fengguo Army in the capital, then governor of Cao.

sentences.zh: 開運初，遷耀州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was moved to defender of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyun he was transferred to defender of Yao.

sentences.zh: 高祖至東京，授洺州刺史，漢球以目疾年高辭郡，帝曰：「廣平小郡，卿臥理有餘，無以疾辭。

translations.literal: When Gaozu reached the Eastern Capital he appointed him Luozhou prefect; Hanqiu declined the commandery on account of eye disease and advanced age; the emperor said: "Guangping is a small commandery—you can govern it lying down with room to spare; do not decline on account of illness."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu reached the Eastern Capital he made him prefect of Luo. Hanqiu pleaded eye trouble and old age. The emperor said, "Guangping is a small prefecture—you can govern it from your couch. Do not refuse because of illness."

sentences.zh: 」至郡未期，復以目疾請代而免。

translations.literal: Before a full term at the commandery he again asked to be replaced because of eye disease and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before his term was out he again asked to be relieved for eye trouble and was excused.

sentences.zh: 乾祐二年秋，卒於京師。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Qianyou he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Qianyou 2 he died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 漢球雖出自行伍，然長於撫理，常以掊斂為戒，民懷其惠，身死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Although Hanqiu came from the ranks of soldiers, he was skilled at soothing governance and always took harsh exaction as a warning; the people cherished his kindness, and on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Though he came from the ranks, Hanqiu excelled at humane governance and shunned harsh levies. The people loved him, and when he died his house held no spare wealth.

sentences.zh: 有管回者，漢球守郡日，辟為判官。

translations.literal: There was one Guan Hui whom Hanqiu, while governing the commandery, had recruited as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: One Guan Hui had served as Hanqiu's deputy while he held the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及漢球卒於汴，回在洺州未之知，一日，忽謂所親曰：「太保遣人召我。

translations.literal: When Hanqiu died at Bian, Hui at Luozhou did not yet know; one day he suddenly told those close to him: "The Grand Guardian has sent for me."
translations.idiomatic: When Hanqiu died at Bian, Hui was still at Luo and knew nothing. One day he suddenly told his intimates, "The Grand Guardian has sent for me."

sentences.zh: 」遂沐浴，新衣冠，無疾瞑目而終。

translations.literal: He then bathed, put on new cap and robes, and without illness closed his eyes and died.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed, dressed in fresh robes, and died peacefully without illness.

sentences.zh: 家人不知其故，後數日，方聞漢球卒。

translations.literal: His family did not know the reason; several days later they learned that Hanqiu had died.
translations.idiomatic: His family did not understand why until, days later, they heard that Hanqiu was dead.

sentences.zh: 張瓘，同州車渡村人，故太原監軍使承業之猶子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Guan was a native of Chedu Village in Tongzhou, the nephew by marriage of the former Taiyuan military supervisor Zhang Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan came from Chedu village in Tongzhou. He was a nephew by marriage of the former Taiyuan military supervisor Zhang Chengye.

sentences.zh: 承業，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: Chengye has a biography in the 《Tang shu》.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye has a biography in the Tang History.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，承業佐唐武皇、莊宗有功，甚見委遇，瓘聞之，與昆仲五人，自故裏奔於太原，莊宗皆任用之。

translations.literal: In the Tianyou era Chengye assisted Tang Wuhuang and Zhuangzong with merit and was greatly entrusted; when Guan heard of it, he and five brothers together fled their homeland to Taiyuan, and Zhuangzong employed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianyou, Chengye aided Tang Wuhuang and Zhuangzong with great merit and won deep trust. When Guan heard of this, he and five brothers left home together for Taiyuan, and Zhuangzong gave them all posts.

sentences.zh: 瓘天祐十三年補麟州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianyou Guan was appointed Lin prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 13 Guan was appointed prefect of Lin.

sentences.zh: 承業治家嚴毅，小過無所容恕，一侄為磁州副使，以其殺河西賣羊客，承業立捕斬之。

translations.literal: Chengye managed his household with stern severity; small faults were not forgiven; one nephew served as deputy at Cizhou and, for killing a Hexi sheep merchant, Chengye immediately had him seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye ran his household with iron discipline and forgave no small fault. A nephew serving as deputy at Ci killed a Hexi sheep trader; Chengye had him seized and beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 常誡瓘等曰：「汝車渡村百姓劉開道下賊，慣作非為，今須改行，若故態不除，死無日矣。

translations.literal: He often admonished Guan and the others: "You Chedu villagers followed the bandit Liu Kaidao in wrongdoing and are used to evil ways; you must reform now—if the old ways are not abandoned, the day of death is not far."
translations.idiomatic: He often warned Guan and his brothers, "You Chedu people followed the bandit Liu Kaidao in wickedness and are used to wrongdoing. Reform now—if you do not drop your old ways, death is near."

sentences.zh: 」故瓘所至不敢誅求。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever Guan went he did not dare to extort.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason Guan never dared to squeeze the districts he governed.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，為密州刺史，秩滿入居環衛。

translations.literal: In the Jin Tianfu era he was Cizhou prefect; when his term ended he entered the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Tianfu he governed Mi. When his term ended he entered the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年夏，卒於官，輟視朝一日。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year of Qianyou he died in office; court audiences were suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Qianyou 3 he died in office, and audiences were halted for a day.

sentences.zh: 李殷，薊州人也。

translations.literal: Li Yin was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin came from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 自後唐莊宗、明宗、晉高祖朝，以偏校遞遷，歷官至檢校司徒，累為郡守。

translations.literal: From the courts of Later Tang Zhuangzong and Mingzong through Jin Gaozu he was promoted in succession from deputy commander and eventually reached honorary Minister of Works, repeatedly holding commandery governorships.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhuangzong and Mingzong of Later Tang through Jin Gaozu he rose from junior officer to honorary Minister of Works, holding one prefecture after another.

sentences.zh: 性沈厚，所蒞無苛暴之名。

translations.literal: His nature was deep and steady; wherever he governed there was no name for harsh cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: He was sober and steady by nature, and none of his postings earned a reputation for cruelty.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝御契丹於澶淵，殷典禁旅，駕還，授鄜州留後，俄加檢校太保。

translations.literal: When Jin Shaodi faced the Khitan at Chanyuan, Yin commanded the palace guard; when the imperial carriage returned he was given Yazhou as acting governor, and soon after was made honorary Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin emperor faced the Khitan at Chanyuan, Yin commanded the palace guard. After the emperor returned he was made acting governor of Yan and soon honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 開運中，授定州節度使，將行，啟少帝曰：「臣之此行，破敵必矣。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era he was appointed military governor of Dingzhou; about to depart, he reported to Shaodi: "On this journey of mine, crushing the enemy is certain."
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun he was made military governor of Dingzhou. Before leaving he told Shaodi, "On this campaign I am sure to break the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆壯其言，及至郡，威略無聞，敵再至，首納降款。

translations.literal: All thought his words bold; when he reached the commandery his prestige and strategy were unheard of; the enemy came again and he was the first to submit terms of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone cheered his boast. At his post he showed neither prestige nor strategy. When the enemy returned he was the first to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 後隨契丹至常山，其將解裏遣殷與契丹首領楊安，同拒我師於洺水，俄而安退，殷以橐裝駝馬遺安。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Khitan to Changshan; the general Jieli sent Yin together with the Khitan leader Yang An to block our army at the Luo River; before long An withdrew, and Yin gave An pack animals, camels, and horses as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the Khitan to Changshan. The general Jieli sent Yin with the Khitan leader Yang An to block our army at the Luo River. Soon An retreated, and Yin gave him baggage camels and horses as gifts.

sentences.zh: 安既北走，殷匿於丘墓獲免，馳以歸我。

translations.literal: When An had fled north, Yin hid among tombs and escaped; he galloped back to submit to us.
translations.idiomatic: When An fled north, Yin hid among graves and survived, then rode back to our side.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其首赴朝闕，及魏州平，以甘陵乏帥，乃命殷為貝州節度使，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised him for being the first to come to the court; when Weizhou was pacified, because Ganling lacked a commander he ordered Yin as military governor of Beizhou and gave him the additional title of honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised him as the first to reach the court. After Weizhou was pacified, with Ganling lacking a commander he made Yin military governor of Beizhou and honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Qianyou he died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he died in office.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太師。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously gave him the title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 劉在明，幽州人。

translations.literal: Liu Zaiming was a native of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zaiming came from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 少有膽氣，本州節度使劉守光用為親信，出為平塞軍使。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and mettle; the circuit military governor Liu Shouguang used him as a trusted intimate and sent him out as commander of Pingsai Army.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold. Liu Shouguang of the circuit made him a confidant and sent him out to command the Pingsai army.

sentences.zh: 守光敗，歸於太原，唐莊宗收為列校。

translations.literal: When Shouguang was defeated he returned to Taiyuan; Tang Zhuangzong took him into the ranks of commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouguang fell, Zaiming went to Taiyuan and Zhuangzong enrolled him among the commanders.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，為捧聖左廂都指揮使，領和州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Mingzong era he was commander of the left wing of the Palsheng Guard and concurrently held the post of Hezhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he commanded the left wing of the Palsheng Guard and also served as prefect of He.

sentences.zh: 從幸汴州，至滎陽，聞朱守殷叛，用為前鋒。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a visit to Bianzhou, when they reached Xingyang and heard that Zhu Shouyin had rebelled, he was used as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial visit to Bian, at Xingyang he heard that Zhu Shouyin had rebelled and was made vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至汴城，率先登城，賊平，授汴州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When they reached Bian city he was the first to scale the wall; when the rebels were pacified he was appointed commander of Bianzhou's horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian he was first over the wall. After the rebels were crushed he became commander of Bian's horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 應順初，為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Yingshun he was made Beizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingshun he was appointed prefect of Bei.

sentences.zh: 明年，移趙州，兼北面行營馬軍都指揮使，以軍戍易州。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to Zhao and concurrently made north-front horse-army commander-in-chief, garrisoning the army at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Zhao, made north-front horse-army commander, and stationed his troops at Yi.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，幽州節度使趙德鈞引軍赴團柏谷，路由易州，取在明軍從。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, the Youzhou military governor Zhao Dejun led his army to Tuanbogu; passing through Yizhou he took Zaiming's army to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai, Zhao Dejun of Youzhou marched to Tuanbogu and, passing Yi, took Zaiming's force with him.

sentences.zh: 及德鈞兵敗，在明奔歸懷州，唐末帝令與萇從簡同守河陽。

translations.literal: When Dejun's army was defeated, Zaiming fled back to Huaizhou; the Tang end emperor ordered him to defend Heyang together with Chang Congjian.
translations.idiomatic: When Dejun was beaten, Zaiming fled to Huai. The last Tang emperor ordered him and Chang Congjian to hold Heyang.

sentences.zh: 晉祖至，乃迎之，京都事定，出為單州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Jin founder arrived, they welcomed him; when the capital was settled, Zaiming went out as Shanzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder came they welcomed him in. After the capital was secure he was sent out as prefect of Shan.

sentences.zh: 天福中，李金全以安州叛，在明從李守貞攻之，大破淮賊，以功授安州防禦使，明年，移絳州。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era Li Jinquan rebelled with Anzhou; Zaiming followed Li Shouzhen to attack and greatly defeated the Huai rebels; for merit he was given Anzhou as defender, and the next year was moved to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, Li Jinquan rebelled at An. Zaiming followed Li Shouzhen, routed the Huai rebels, and was made defender of An, then moved to Jiang the next year.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠據青州叛，召為行營馬步軍都指揮使，領齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan held Qingzhou in rebellion and Zaiming was summoned as camp horse-and-foot commander-in-chief and concurrently defender of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled at Qingzhou, Zaiming was called up as camp horse-and-foot commander and defender of Qi.

sentences.zh: 青州平，遷相州留後，歷邢州、晉州留後。

translations.literal: When Qingzhou was pacified he was transferred as acting governor of Xiangzhou and successively held acting governorships of Xing and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After Qingzhou fell he became acting governor of Xiang, then held acting posts at Xing and Jin.

translations.literal: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：契丹犯闕，建雄留後劉在明朝於契丹，以節度副使駱知朗知州事。）〉

translations.literal: (Zizhi tongjian: When the Khitan violated the capital, Jianxiong acting governor Liu Zaiming submitted to the Khitan and had the deputy military governor Luo Zhilang manage prefectural affairs.)
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: When the Khitan invaded the capital, Liu Zaiming of Jianxiong submitted to them and put Deputy Military Governor Luo Zhilang in charge of the prefecture.)

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，授幽州道行營都部署。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zaiming was appointed overall commander of the Youzhou campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he made Zaiming overall commander on the Youzhou front.

sentences.zh: 時契丹守中山，在明出師經略，契丹乃棄城而去，遂授鎮州留後。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan held Zhongshan; Zaiming led his army in planning and the Khitan then abandoned the city and left, and he was given Zhenzhou as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then held Zhongshan. Zaiming marched against them, the Khitan abandoned the city, and he was made acting governor of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年五月，正授鎮州節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Qianyou he was formally appointed military governor of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Qianyou 1 he was formally made military governor of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 六月，以疾卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he died of illness at his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he died of illness in office.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 馬萬，澶州人也。

translations.literal: Ma Wan was a native of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wan came from Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少從軍，善水遊。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the army and was skilled at swimming.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he joined the army and was an expert swimmer.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗與梁軍對壘於河上，莊宗於德勝渡夾河立南北寨。

translations.literal: Tang Zhuangzong and the Liang army faced each other on the Yellow River; Zhuangzong at Desheng Ford set up north and south stockades on both banks of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong faced the Liang army on the Yellow River and built paired north and south camps at Desheng Ford.

sentences.zh: 會梁軍急攻南寨，於中流聯戰艦以絕援路，晝夜攻城者三日，寨將氏延賞告急於莊宗。

translations.literal: The Liang army urgently attacked the south stockade and in midstream linked warships to cut off the route of relief; for three days and nights they assaulted the city; the stockade commander Shi Yanshang reported the emergency to Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang pressed the south camp hard, chained warships in the stream to block relief, and assaulted it day and night for three days. Commander Shi Yanshang sent word to Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗隔河望敵，無如之何，乃召人能水遊破賊者。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong looked across the river at the enemy and could do nothing about it; he then summoned anyone who could swim through the water to break the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong watched the enemy from the far bank, helpless, and called for anyone who could swim through and break them.

sentences.zh: 時萬兄弟皆應募，遂潛行入南寨，往來者三，又助燒船艦，汴軍遂退。

translations.literal: At that time Wan and his brothers all answered the call; they then slipped into the south stockade, went back and forth three times, and also helped burn the warships, and the Bian army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and his brothers volunteered. They swam into the south camp three times, helped burn the Liang ships, and the Bian army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 由此升為水軍小校，漸典禁軍，遙領刺史，累遷奉國左廂都指揮使、泗州防禦使。

translations.literal: From this he was promoted to junior officer of the water army, gradually held posts in the palace guard, held prefectures in title only, and was successively promoted to commander of the left wing of the Fengguo Guard and defender of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this he rose in the water forces, entered the palace guard, held titular prefectures, and eventually commanded the left wing of the Fengguo Guard while defending Si.

sentences.zh: 晉天福二年夏，範延光叛於鄴，牙將孫銳率兵至黎陽，朝廷遣侍衛馬軍都指揮使白奉進領兵渡滑州，萬亦預其行。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Jin Tianfu, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye; his officer Sun Rui led troops to Liyang; the court sent the palace horse-army commander Bai Fengjin to lead troops across Huazhou, and Wan also took part in the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jin Tianfu 2, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye. Sun Rui marched to Liyang. The court sent Bai Fengjin across Huazhou, and Wan went with him.

sentences.zh: 時滑州節度使符彥饒潛通鄴下，殺白奉進於牙署。

translations.literal: At that time the Huazhou military governor Fu Yanrao secretly communicated with Ye and killed Bai Fengjin in the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: The Huazhou governor Fu Yanrao was secretly in league with Ye and murdered Bai Fengjin in headquarters.

sentences.zh: 萬領本軍兵士將助亂，會奉國右廂都指揮使盧順密亦以兵至，諭以逆順，萬不得已，與順密急趨公府，執彥饒生送闕下。

translations.literal: Wan was about to lead his own troops to join the disorder when the Fengguo right-wing commander Lu Shunmi also arrived with troops and instructed him in loyalty and rebellion; Wan had no choice but to hurry with Shunmi to the government office and seize Yanrao alive to send to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was ready to join the mutiny when Lu Shunmi of the Fengguo right wing arrived, argued duty and treason, and forced Wan to rush with him to the government compound, seize Yanrao alive, and send him to court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷即以萬為滑州節度使，而盧順密酬之甚淺。

translations.literal: The court then appointed Wan military governor of Huazhou, while Lu Shunmi's reward was very slight.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Wan military governor of Hua, but rewarded Shunmi meagerly.

sentences.zh: 居無何，晉高祖稍知其事，即以順密為涇州兵馬留後，漸薄於萬。

translations.literal: Before long Jin Gaozu gradually learned of the matter and made Shunmi acting Jingzhou army commander, gradually treating Wan less favorably.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gaozu learned what had happened, gave Shunmi the Jingzhou army post, and began to slight Wan.

sentences.zh: 萬鎮鄧州，未幾罷鎮，授上將軍，以目疾致仕。

translations.literal: Wan governed Dengzhou; before long he was removed from his command and given the title of Senior General, retiring on account of eye disease.
translations.idiomatic: Wan governed Deng, was soon removed, made Senior General, and retired for eye trouble.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年四月卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Qianyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Qianyou 3 he died.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝一日。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: Audiences were halted for a day.

sentences.zh: 李彥從，字士元，汾州孝義人。

translations.literal: Li Yancong, styled Shiyuan, was a native of Xiaoyi in Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yancong, courtesy name Shiyuan, came from Xiaoyi in Fen.

sentences.zh: 父德，麟州司馬。

translations.literal: His father De was Sima of Linzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li De was Sima of Lin.

sentences.zh: 彥從少習武藝，出行伍間，高祖典禁軍，以鄉里之舊，任為親信。

translations.literal: Yancong in youth practiced martial arts and moved among the ranks; when Gaozu commanded the palace guard, because of their old ties from the same district he was employed as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in arms young and served in the ranks. When Gaozu commanded the guard, their hometown tie made Yancong a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 國初，用為左飛龍使、檢校司空。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was used as Left Flying Dragon envoy and honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he became Left Flying Dragon envoy and honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 鎮州逐敵之際，請兵於朝廷，高祖令彥從率軍赴之。

translations.literal: At the time of driving the enemy from Zhenzhou, troops were requested from the court; Gaozu ordered Yancong to lead an army there.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzhou needed troops to drive off the enemy, Gaozu sent Yancong at the head of an army.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，領恩州刺史。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Qianyou he held the post of Enzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he was prefect of En.

sentences.zh: 趙暉討王景崇於岐下，彥從為兵馬都監，破川軍有功，賊平，授濮州刺史，治有政能，百姓悅之。

translations.literal: Zhao Hui attacked Wang Jingchong at Qixia; Yancong was army supervisor and broke the Chuan army with merit; when the rebels were pacified he was given Puzhou prefect; his governance had political ability and the people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hui besieged Wang Jingchong below Qi. Yancong served as army supervisor, defeated the Chuan force, and after the rebels fell was made prefect of Pu, where his rule pleased the people.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬，卒於郡。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Qianyou he died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Qianyou 3 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 白再榮，本蕃部人也。

translations.literal: Bai Zairong was originally a man of the tribal frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zairong was originally from the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 少從軍，累遷護聖左廂指揮使。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the army and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the left wing of the Husheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the army young and rose to command the left wing of the Husheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 晉末，契丹入汴，明年，契丹主北去，再榮從部帳至真定。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin the Khitan entered Bian; the next year when the Khitan ruler went north, Zairong followed the tribal encampment to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jin the Khitan took Bian. The next year, when the Khitan ruler withdrew north, Zairong followed the tribal camp to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 其年閏七月晦，李筠、何福晉相率殺北帥滿達勒，據甲仗庫，敵勢未退，筠等使人召再榮。

translations.literal: On the last day of the intercalary seventh month of that year, Li Jun and He Fujin together led the killing of the northern commander Mandale, seized the armory, and the enemy's strength had not yet withdrawn; Jun and the others sent someone to summon Zairong.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the intercalary seventh month, Li Jun and He Fujin killed the northern commander Mandale and seized the armory. The enemy had not yet retreated, and they sent for Zairong.

sentences.zh: 再榮端坐本營，遲疑久之。

translations.literal: Zairong sat upright in his own camp and hesitated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong sat stiffly in camp and hesitated a long while.

sentences.zh: 為軍吏所迫，乃行。

translations.literal: Pressed by the army clerks, he then went.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by his officers, he finally went.

sentences.zh: 翊日，逐出床答勒，諸軍以再榮名次在諸校之右，乃請權知留後事。

translations.literal: The next day they drove out Chuangdale; the armies, because Zairong's seniority ranked above the various commanders, then asked him to act as temporary manager of the acting governorship.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they expelled Chuangdale. Because Zairong outranked the other commanders, the troops asked him to act as temporary governor.

translations.literal: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·李筠傳》：筠請馮道領節度，道曰：「予主奏事而已，留後事當議功臣為之。

translations.literal: (Dongdu shilue, Biography of Li Jun: Jun asked Feng Dao to take the governorship. Dao said, "I am in charge of memorial affairs only; the acting governorship should be discussed and given to a meritorious officer."
translations.idiomatic: (Dongdu shilue, Biography of Li Jun: Jun asked Feng Dao to take the governorship. Dao said, "I only handle memorials to the throne; the acting post should go to a meritorious officer after discussion."

sentences.zh: 」以諸將之甲者為留後。）〉

translations.literal: " The one among the generals with the strongest armor was made acting governor.)
translations.idiomatic: " The commander with the finest armor was made acting governor.)

sentences.zh: 再榮貪昧無決，舉止多疑，出入騎從，露刃註矢，諸校不相統攝，互有猜貳。

translations.literal: Zairong was greedy and dim without decision; his conduct was full of suspicion; when he went out his mounted followers bore bared blades and notched arrows; the various commanders did not command one another and mutually harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong was greedy, indecisive, and suspicious. His escort rode with naked blades and strung arrows. The commanders would not obey one another and eyed each other with distrust.

sentences.zh: 奉國廂主王饒懼為再榮所並，乃據東門樓，以兵自衛，偽稱足疾，不敢見再榮。

translations.literal: The Fengguo wing commander Wang Rao feared being absorbed by Zairong and therefore held the east gate tower with troops to protect himself, falsely claiming foot ailment and not daring to see Zairong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rao of the Fengguo wing feared Zairong would swallow his command, held the east gate tower with troops, and pretended foot trouble to avoid meeting him.

sentences.zh: 司天監趙延乂俱與之善，乃來往解釋，遂無相忌之意。

translations.literal: The Director of the Astronomy Bureau Zhao Yanyi was on good terms with both of them and came and went to explain matters, and thus there was no mutual suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanyi of the Astronomy Bureau, friendly with both men, shuttled between them until suspicion eased.

sentences.zh: 再榮以李崧、和凝攜家在彼，令軍士數百人環迫崧、凝，以求賞給，崧、凝各出家財與之。

translations.literal: Zairong, because Li Song and He Ning had brought their families there, ordered several hundred soldiers to surround and press Song and Ning to demand reward payments; Song and Ning each gave their household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Song and He Ning had families in the city, Zairong ringed them with hundreds of soldiers demanding payment. Both men paid from their private wealth.

sentences.zh: 再榮欲害崧以利其財，前磁州刺史李穀謂再榮曰：「公與諸將為契丹所擄，淩辱萬端，旦夕憂死。

translations.literal: Zairong wished to kill Song to profit by his wealth; the former Cizhou prefect Li Gu said to Zairong: "You and the generals were captured by the Khitan, insulted in ten thousand ways, and feared death morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong wanted to kill Song for his money. Li Gu, former prefect of Ci, said, "You and the other officers were Khitan captives, humiliated beyond measure, expecting death at any hour.

sentences.zh: 今日眾力逐出蕃戎，鎮民死者不下三千人，豈獨公等之功！

translations.literal: Today by the crowd's strength you drove out the barbarian troops; of the town's people no fewer than three thousand died—how is that the merit of you alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Today you drove the barbarians out by mass effort. No fewer than three thousand townspeople died—is that yours alone!"

sentences.zh: 才得生路，便擬殺一宰相，他日到闕，儻有所問，何以為辭？

translations.literal: You have just gained the road to life and already plan to kill a chief minister; when you reach the court, if there is some question—what answer will you give?"
translations.idiomatic: You have barely won your lives and already mean to kill a chief minister. At court, if anyone asks, what will you say?"

sentences.zh: 」再榮默然。

translations.literal: Zairong was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong said nothing.

sentences.zh: 再榮又欲括率在城居民家財，以給軍士，李穀又譬解之，乃止。

translations.literal: Zairong again wished to seize and inventory the household wealth of residents in the city to give to the soldiers; Li Gu again explained and dissuaded him, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong next wanted to strip the townspeople's wealth for the troops. Li Gu talked him out of it again.

sentences.zh: 其漢人曾事滿達勒者盡拘之，以取其財。

translations.literal: All Han people who had once served Mandale were detained to take their wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Every Han who had served Mandale was seized and robbed.

sentences.zh: 高祖以再榮為鎮州留後，為政貪虐難狀，鎮人呼為「白麻答」。

translations.literal: Gaozu made Zairong acting governor of Zhenzhou; his governance was greedy and cruel beyond description, and the people of the command called him "White Mandale."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made Zairong acting governor of Zhen. His rule was greedily brutal beyond words, and the people called him "White Mandale."

sentences.zh: 未幾，移授滑州節度使，箕斂誅求，民不聊生，乃征還京師。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred as military governor of Huazhou; he extorted and demanded ruthlessly until the people could not live; he was then summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to Hua as military governor, squeezed the people mercilessly, and was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周太祖入京城，軍士攻再榮之第，迫脅再榮，盡取財貨既，軍士前啟曰：「某等軍健，常趨事麾下，一旦無禮至此，今後何顏謁見？

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital, soldiers attacked Zairong's residence and coerced Zairong; after they had taken all his goods and wealth, the soldiers stepped forward and said: "We soldiers and laborers always hurried to serve under Your Excellency; once we have been this rude, what face have we to meet you afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital, troops stormed Zairong's house and robbed him. When everything was taken, one soldier said, "We always served under you, sir. After this disgrace, how can we face you again?"

sentences.zh: 」即奮刃擊之，挈其首而去，後家人以帛贖葬之。

translations.literal: They then flourished their blades and struck him, carried off his head and left; later his family redeemed it with silk for burial.
translations.idiomatic: They hacked off his head and carried it away. Later his family bought the head back with silk for burial.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉、漢之際，有以懋軍功、勤王事、取旌旄符竹者多矣，其間有及民之惠者無幾焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: In the transition between Jin and Han, many won merit through military achievement, labored in loyal service to the throne, and took banners, tallies, and bamboo commissions—but among them those who brought kindness to the people were few.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Between Jin and Han many men won merit in war, served the throne loyally, and took commissions—but few brought real kindness to the people.

sentences.zh: 如王周之閫政、審交之民譽，蓋其優者也；

translations.literal: Such as Wang Zhou's governance of a circuit and Shenjiao's praise from the people—these were among the best;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou's circuit rule and Shenjiao's popular praise were among the best cases.

sentences.zh: 漢球、張瓘抑又次焉。

translations.literal: Hanqiu and Zhang Guan were again a step below them.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiu and Zhang Guan stood a rank below even those.

sentences.zh: 是宜紀之篇以示來者，其餘皆不足觀也已。

translations.literal: These deserve to be recorded in the chapters to show those who come after; the rest are not worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Such men deserve record in these pages for posterity; the rest are hardly worth notice.

sentences.zh: 張鵬以一言之失，遽滅其身，亦足誡後代多言橫議之徒歟！

translations.literal: Zhang Peng, through one word's fault, suddenly lost his life—this too is enough to warn later generations of those who talk much and argue recklessly!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Peng lost his life over a single ill-chosen word—enough warning for later generations of men who talk too much and argue rashly!
